If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle your privacy differently? Most of us would. We would be more careful about which services we used and what information we shared. Since a time machine doesn't exist, we have to face the reality of the present — your personal data is being publicly sold right now.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, and even family relationships are being packaged and sold to marketers, insurance companies, and hackers. While Safari and Mail's built-in Apple privacy protections can block some tracking as you browse the web, they cannot retrieve information that has been collected over the years and distributed to hundreds of broker databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion dollar industry by collecting your digital data, packaging it, and selling it. It's time to take your personal data off the market and the internet. Let's look at how to do that.

The security risks of the data broker business

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying scam calls. When your information is everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyber threats. Since this industry is barely regulated, your most private information and details — including past employers and residences, previous loan records, and more — are available for purchase at any time. This poses a massive security concern.

Modern scammers use broker data to gather and carefully craft highly personalised (and hard-to-detect) phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, where you live, or the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your instinctive defences. If a scammer knows a great deal about you, they only need to strike when your guard is down to greatly increase their chances of success.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function like publicly searchable databases, serving as tools for stalkers and harassers. By mapping out the relationship networks between your relatives, friends, and neighbours, brokers provide a blueprint for locating people who intend to keep their privacy and deliberately hide their whereabouts.

The solution: use Incogni to automatically remove your data

The scale of this ecosystem is staggering, and frankly, disheartening. Trying to request the removal of your data from hundreds of websites one by one is almost a futile effort even as a full-time job, because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that knows the ins and outs of this industry and how to defend your privacy rights.

That's exactly why a service like Incogni is essential to your life — both in the digital world and the real world. This service turns your enormous problem (data being everywhere and being sold) into a solved one, handling it in a one-stop-shop approach. Incogni handles the tedious, repetitive administrative paperwork of opt-out requests on your behalf automatically, so you don't have to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one. They ensure your data is not only removed once, but stays removed, preventing brokers from sneaking back in to recollect it.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your personal data removal in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may contain your information
  • Removal requests being sent out on your behalf
  • Items that have been removed and are being continuously followed up on

The real benefits of data removal for privacy-conscious individuals

Being scrubbed from internet broker databases can deliver immediate benefits for you and your family

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts will decrease.
  • Scammers lose their leads. Identity thieves often obtain victim information from broker websites.
  • Your personal address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to easily find where you live.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, as limited data exposure reduces the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial health.
